key_insight: ASCENT reveals a gap between answering complete medical vignettes and revising diagnostic impressions as information arrives, while targeted fine-tuning improves stepwise performance.
clinical_relevance: Evaluating intermediate impressions may better reflect clinical information flow than final-answer accuracy alone, but these results do not establish clinical readiness.
method: Built 3,078 clinician-annotated stepwise problems from MedQA-USMLE.
Organized vignettes into EMR-aligned Findings, Impression, and supporting Rationale steps.
Evaluated LLMs, fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B and 32B, and tested robustness and rollout behavior.
evidence_signal: ASCENT fine-tuning improved F1 over pre-trained and HuatuoGPT-o1 CoT-trained baselines, primarily through precision gains; strong MedQA-USMLE performance did not eliminate stepwise reasoning gaps.
watch_item: Error propagation during rollout remains a key concern, and performance on benchmark-derived cases does not establish safety in real clinical workflows.
paper_title: ASCENT: A Benchmark for Evaluating and Advancing Stepwise Diagnostic Reasoning in Large Language Models on Common Clinical Scenarios
